subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Marie Curie discovered the element radium in 1898.
• Radium emits powerful radioactive energy that can penetrate human tissue.
• Curie initially believed that radium's energy could be harnessed as a general health tonic.
• The discovery of radium proved essential to the development of cancer treatment through radiation therapy.
• Radiation therapy has saved millions of lives by targeting and destroying cancer cells.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the significance of Curie's discovery. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Curie first discovered radium, an element that she believed could be harnessed as a general health tonic, in 1898.
choices.B: In 1898, Curie discovered the element radium, which emits powerful radioactive energy that can penetrate human tissue.
choices.C: Though her discovery of radium was essential to developing cancer treatment, Curie initially believed that the element could be used as a general health tonic.
choices.D: Curie's 1898 discovery of radium proved essential to developing cancer treatment through radiation therapy, which has saved millions of lives by targeting and destroying cancer cells.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes the significance of Curie's discovery, noting that it proved essential to developing cancer treatment through radiation therapy, which has saved millions of lives by targeting and destroying cancer cells.
